solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rugby player in Texan city with former chancellor of the exchequer

parts.note: Austin is the state capital of Texas
Denis Healey was Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A rugby star is seen in Texas alongside a retired British finance minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin Healey is a former England rugby player; the answer is also a classic British sports car, fitting the puzzle's car theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin Healey played scrum-half and wing for England and Leicester Tigers, so the full name identifies a rugby player.

clue.text: Sort of salesman running crusade

indicators.note: running in the sense of operating or in motion, so the letters of crusade are set going into a new order

explanation.surface: A salesman runs a crusade, campaigning hard for his wares.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-hand motor trader is proverbially a type of salesman, the stock figure of the slick car dealer.

clue.text: Wins with his trump playing

indicators.note: the letters of his trump are put into play and reshuffled, as cards are in a game

explanation.surface: A card player takes the tricks by playing his trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Victories or successes are wins; as a verb it also means prevails, so both readings match.

clue.text: Knob crashed one pick-up!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the selected letters are read from bottom to top
pick means select a run of letters from inside the words crashed one

explanation.surface: A knob on a vehicle smashed in a crash involving a pick-up truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick-up' does two jobs: 'pick' selects the letters spanning 'crashed one', and 'up' turns them upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot or swelling on a stem or body part is a lump or knob, the anatomical and botanical sense.

clue.text: Lovely intonation in engine, mostly reconditioned

indicators.note: the word in places one piece within the other
an engine that is reconditioned is rebuilt, so the remaining letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of engine is used

parts.note: a chant is an intoned song or recitation

explanation.surface: A mechanic admires the sweet note of a mostly rebuilt engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engine, mostly' gives ENGIN, which 'reconditioned' rearranges to ENING; CHANT goes inside after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charming or delightful is lovely, a straightforward adjective synonym.

clue.text: Sitting cross-legged in this car, is in pain initially — too awkward

parts.note: Lotus is a British sports-car maker

indicators.note: awkward signals that the letters are put in an ungainly, jumbled order
initially means take only the opening letter of pain

explanation.surface: Folding yourself cross-legged into a tiny sports car is painful and far too awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges IS IN plus P and TOO into POSITION.
explanation.definitionFit: The yoga posture in which one sits with each foot resting on the opposite thigh is this cross-legged seated pose.

clue.text: Going uphill, say, a horse-drawn cart's distance covered?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means the assembled letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: say is the usual signal for e.g., for example
a dray is a low horse-drawn cart, traditionally for brewers' barrels

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn cart toils uphill, and someone wonders how far it has travelled.
explanation.walkthrough: EG + A + DRAY makes EGADRAY, which 'Going uphill' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: Length measured in yards, as gained in American football or golf, is ground or distance covered.

clue.text: Having a particular aura, a motel with hip cars shown off

indicators.note: off suggests disorder or being knocked out of place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trendy motel shows off its fashionable cars to guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is A MOTEL and HIP CARS together; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessing a distinctive mood or feeling is to be full of ambience, the figurative sense of the adjective.

clue.text: One that provides compression for old car with engine at back and large boot?

indicators.note: for here means the compressor is supplied for the car, so it is attached after it

parts.words: old car with engine at back
parts.note: the original Volkswagen Beetle had its engine in the rear
a crusher squashes or compresses things

explanation.surface: A crusher compacts an old Beetle at the scrapyard; the boot joke hints at a car's luggage space.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'boot' is British for a car's trunk, which misleads; here it is footwear. The clue gives the pieces in reverse order: the crusher comes 'for' the Beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous slang for a big heavy shoe or a large foot, especially a policeman's, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Twelve horrid characters messed up a popular song

indicators.note: messed up means the twelve letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Twelve nasty people make a mess of a favourite tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' is a link: the letters of Twelve horrid are the characters messed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known Irish folk ballad, a pub singalong standard, so it is a popular song.

clue.text: Citroen manoeuvred, with just one change of direction, in a circle exclusively

indicators.note: a car being manoeuvred is moved about, so the letters are shifted into a new order

indicators.text: with just one change of direction
indicators.note: one compass point swaps for another: N for north becomes E for east

explanation.surface: A Citroen is steered round, turning only once, inside a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: CITROEN with its N changed to E gives CITROEE, which 'manoeuvred' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A small exclusive group of people with shared interests is a clique, a closed social circle.

clue.text: Body that regulates on family content over media, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the leading letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A watchdog rules on family-friendly content across the media.
explanation.walkthrough: Ofcom is the UK's communications regulator, overseeing broadcasting and telecoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Office of Communications is the British statutory body regulating broadcasting, telecoms and postal services.

clue.text: Get a handle on computer-aided manufacturing for car part

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: the shaft of a tool is its handle

explanation.surface: An engineer tries to understand computerised production methods for making vehicle components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a handle on' looks like an idiom for understanding; only 'handle' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine component, a rotating rod with lobes that opens and closes the valves, so a car part.

clue.text: Part of the Roman Diet of Worms, in Italy

definitions.text: Part of the Roman Diet of Worms, in Italy

parts.words: Part of the Roman Diet of Worms, in Italy
parts.note: the Diet of Worms was a 1521 imperial assembly; here diet means food and worms are little noodles eaten in Rome

explanation.surface: A history note about the Diet of Worms, the council that tried Luther.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diet of Worms was a council held in the German city of Worms; here 'Diet' is food, and the answer's name means 'little worms' in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin pasta, eaten in Italy, takes its name from the Italian for little worms.

clue.text: Old manuscripts from Chile, by the one writing in undies

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces within the outer word

parts.note: pants are underpants, informally undies
RCH is Chile's international vehicle registration code
the writer of a clue refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: Old documents from Chile were apparently smuggled in someone's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: RCH is the letter code on Chilean cars abroad, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal skins prepared for writing on were used for ancient documents, so the plural names old manuscripts.

clue.text: No more than some Renaults have it

indicators.note: have it means the words contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Only a few Renault cars have this feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'some' and the start of 'Renaults'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, the word means nothing more than or only, as in a trifling amount.

clue.text: See 6
Rear light not right? Outside Britain, they make it count

definitions.text: Outside Britain, they make it count

indicators.note: not means the following word's letters are removed

parts.note: these words are the fodder for the deletion; that the result also runs forwards inside them is a coincidence of the letters removed
taken as the word itself, its letters lifted out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A rear light isn't working properly, and drivers abroad must make it count.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters R, I, G, H, T are removed one by one from REARLIGHT, leaving EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: A British nobleman of this rank corresponds to a count elsewhere in Europe, so foreigners give him that title.

clue.text: Posh car going round ring road, with Greek character turning up speakers here?

indicators.note: going round means the car encircles the next pieces

parts.note: RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the archetypal posh car
O is ring-shaped
ST, street, stands in for road

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce circles a ring road while a Greek turns up to address the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh car' is the usual crossword shorthand for a Rolls-Royce; 'ring road' looks like one thing but splits into ring and road.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for public speaking is where orators stand, hence where speakers are found.

clue.text: Group of people in one car out by river

indicators.note: in places the people inside the rearranged letters
out means the letters of one car are knocked out of order

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: A group squeezes into one car and drives out to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE CAR rearranged by 'out' gives ACORNE; MEN goes inside after its first letter, then R is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster of fervent worshippers who sit near a church pulpit and call out responses, thus a group of devotees.

clue.text: Chart-topper, a bit offensive and possibly harmful

parts.note: a chart-topper is number one, written No. 1 with the 1 read as I
some means a bit or a certain amount

explanation.surface: A chart-topping song is a bit offensive and maybe harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: NO. 1 becomes NOI, the digit 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a smell that is disgusting and unwholesome or noxious, so offensive and harmful.

clue.text: Tell vehicle has been tailed during this month

indicators.note: during means one piece sits inside the time span named by the other

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is an old business abbreviation for this month

indicators.note: tailed means the last letter has been cut off

parts.note: a truck is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a vehicle has been followed this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailed' looks like being followed by police; here it means docked of its tail, the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct or order someone is to tell them what to do, a verb synonym.

clue.text: See 10
One to contest tip from social climbers

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to vie is to compete or contest

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, so take the initial of social

explanation.surface: Someone contests a hint picked up from ambitious social climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social climbers' looks like one phrase; 'social' gives S and 'climbers' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen climbing plants that cling to walls and trees, so in the plural they are climbers.

clue.text: Part of this crossword where cars are found, for a start

definitions.meaning: the pattern of black and white squares makes up the puzzle

definitions.text: where cars are found, for a start
definitions.meaning: at the beginning of a motor race the cars line up on the starting ...

explanation.definitionFit: The pattern of squares in a puzzle and the marked starting positions on a racetrack share this name.

clue.text: Appearance of a competitor, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be spoken aloud for their sound

parts.note: a competitor is a rival, so the phrase spoken gives a rival

explanation.surface: A competitor turns up on the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning up or coming on the scene is an appearance, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Underground part of plant Mercedes-Benz vacated has endless heroin supply

indicators.note: supply read as supplely, nimbly bent into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
vacated means emptied, so only the first and last letters of Mercedes-Benz remain
endless means the final letter of heroin is dropped

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler stashes a heroin supply in an empty Mercedes.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercedes-Benz emptied leaves M and Z; heroin without its end gives HEROI; 'supply' rearranges these seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal underground stem that sends out roots and shoots, as in ginger or iris, is a plant part below ground.

clue.text: Sleep with old Arts & Crafts man first, perhaps one involved in folk movement

definitions.text: perhaps one involved in folk movement

indicators.note: first means the Arts and Crafts man comes before the other piece

parts.note: William Morris led the Victorian Arts and Crafts movement
Wayne Sleep is a famous British ballet dancer

explanation.surface: A sleep with an old craftsman beforehand: a folk dancer's lazy afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep' is Wayne Sleep, a well-known British ballet dancer, not a nap. Morris dancing is traditional English folk dancing with bells and sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in this traditional English folk dance is one taking part in a folk movement, punning on dance moves.
